title: Given a Scenario, Install Applications According to Requirements

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Application installation requires more than launching an installer. Verify operating-system compatibility, hardware requirements, external devices, distribution method, and deployment impact before proceeding.
The main mental model is: compatibility → hardware → distribution → impact → install.
bullets: Graphics, VRAM, RAM, CPU, token, and storage requirements
Physical media, mountable ISO, downloadable package, and image deployment
Device, network, operational, and business impact

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Before installing an application, can you determine whether the device meets its requirements and choose a deployment method that avoids technical and business problems?
bullets: Physical authentication or licensing → hardware token

sections.title: System Requirements for Applications
paragraphs: Applications publish minimum and recommended requirements. Unsupported installations may fail, crash, perform poorly, omit features, or leave the organization without vendor support.
sections.callout: Read and verify the full requirements before installing.

sections.title: 32-bit vs. 64-bit Dependent Application Requirements
paragraphs: Applications may target 32-bit or 64-bit architecture. A 64-bit application generally needs a supported 64-bit operating environment; vendor compatibility must be verified rather than assumed.
sections.callout: Application architecture must match an operating environment the vendor supports.

sections.title: Graphics and VRAM Requirements

entries.title: Dedicated vs. Integrated Graphics Card
paragraphs: Integrated graphics is built into the platform and shares system resources. A dedicated graphics card supplies separate graphics-processing hardware and typically its own graphics memory. CAD, 3D rendering, gaming, and video production may require a supported dedicated GPU.
entries.recognitionCue: A professional 3D application requires a supported discrete GPU → dedicated graphics.

entries.title: Video Random-Access Memory (VRAM) Requirements
paragraphs: VRAM is memory used by the graphics processor. Applications can specify a minimum VRAM capacity independently of system RAM.
entries.recognitionCue: The requirement describes memory available to the GPU → VRAM.

sections.callout: RAM supports the system and applications; VRAM supports graphics processing.

entries.title: RAM Requirements
paragraphs: Insufficient system RAM can cause installation restrictions, heavy paging, poor performance, and application instability.
entries.memoryHook: RAM = working space for running applications.

entries.title: Central Processing Unit (CPU) Requirements
paragraphs: Applications may require a supported processor architecture, performance level, instruction set, or core count.
entries.recognitionCue: The processor architecture is unsupported → CPU requirement not met.

entries.title: External Hardware Tokens
paragraphs: Some applications require a physical token or USB dongle for authentication, security, or licensing.
entries.recognitionCue: Software will not run without its USB security device → external hardware token.

entries.title: Storage Requirements
paragraphs: Plan for installer files, the installed application, updates, temporary data, and user-generated content—not just the initial download size.
entries.recognitionCue: The application needs 30 GB but only 8 GB is free → storage requirement not met.

sections.title: Application-to-OS Compatibility
paragraphs: Confirm that the vendor supports the installed Windows, macOS, or Linux release and the required architecture. Powerful hardware does not compensate for an unsupported operating system.
sections.callout: Hardware compatibility and operating-system compatibility are separate checks.

entries.title: Physical Media vs. Mountable ISO File
paragraphs: Physical media is a tangible disc or USB device. An ISO is a disk-image file that the operating system mounts so it behaves like inserted optical media.
entries.memoryHook: Hold it → physical. Mount it → ISO.
entries.recognitionCue: An .iso opens as a virtual disc → mountable ISO.

entries.title: Downloadable Package
paragraphs: An installer may be downloaded from an authorized vendor site, application repository, or corporate portal. Verify the source before installation.
entries.recognitionCue: The installer is obtained online as a package → downloadable package.

entries.title: Image Deployment
paragraphs: Organizations can include applications in a standardized system image for consistent deployment to many devices.
entries.recognitionCue: Deploy the same approved application set at scale → image deployment.

sections.title: Impact Considerations for New Applications
paragraphs: A deployment plan must look beyond whether setup completes. Evaluate the endpoint, network, daily operations, and organizational consequences.

entries.title: Device
paragraphs: Consider CPU, RAM, storage, graphics, battery life, and overall endpoint performance.
entries.recognitionCue: The installed application makes the workstation unusably slow → device impact.

entries.title: Network
paragraphs: Consider installer downloads, updates, synchronization, cloud traffic, streaming, and simultaneous deployments.
entries.recognitionCue: A mass push saturates the WAN → network impact.

entries.title: Operation
paragraphs: Consider reboots, downtime, conflicts, training, and workflow disruption.
entries.recognitionCue: Required reboots interrupt employees during business hours → operational impact.

entries.title: Business
paragraphs: Consider licensing cost, compliance, security, productivity, risk, and business-process effects.
entries.recognitionCue: Licensing exceeds the approved budget → business impact.

sections.callout: PC → device. Traffic → network. Workflow → operation. Organization, cost, or risk → business.

sections.title: Application Installation Workflow
bullets: Verify CPU, RAM, VRAM, storage, and graphics requirements.
Choose physical media, ISO, downloadable package, or image deployment.
Assess device, network, operational, and business impact.
Install only after requirements and authorization are satisfied.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: USB security dongle → external hardware token
Actual disc or USB → physical media
Cost, compliance, or organizational risk → business impact

entries.title: RAM vs. VRAM
paragraphs: RAM is general system memory; VRAM is graphics-processor memory.

entries.title: Dedicated vs. Integrated Graphics
paragraphs: Integrated graphics shares platform resources; dedicated graphics provides separate processing hardware and typically dedicated VRAM.

entries.title: Hardware vs. OS Compatibility
paragraphs: Meeting hardware requirements does not mean the vendor supports the installed OS. Verify both.

entries.title: Physical Media vs. ISO
paragraphs: Physical media is an actual device or disc; an ISO is a mountable file representing media contents.

entries.title: Image vs. Downloadable Package
paragraphs: An image provides a standardized environment at scale; a downloadable package is a separate application installer.

entries.title: Device vs. Operational Impact
paragraphs: Computer performance is device impact; employee downtime and workflow disruption are operational impact.

entries.title: Network vs. Business Impact
paragraphs: Bandwidth use is network impact; licensing, compliance, cost, and organizational risk are business impact.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Cost, risk, or compliance → business impact
